question: What is the primary target site for medication administered via the intrathecal route?
explanation: Intrathecal medication is delivered directly into the cerebrospinal fluid within the subarachnoid space. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why are drug doses typically much smaller when given intrathecally compared to orally?

options.A: The liver breaks down the medicine much faster in the spinal cord
options.B: The stomach acid destroys most of the oral medication before absorption
options.C: The drug goes directly to the central nervous system without being filtered first
options.D: The blood-brain barrier absorbs most of the drug before it works

explanation: Delivering medication straight to the cerebrospinal fluid bypasses systemic circulation and barriers, requiring less drug to achieve the desired effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h1)

question: Between which two meningeal layers is the subarachnoid space located?
explanation: The subarachnoid space sits specifically between the middle arachnoid layer and the innermost pia mater layer. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: At which spinal level is an intrathecal injection usually performed in adults to avoid damaging the spinal cord?
explanation: In adults, the spinal cord ends around the L1-L2 vertebra, so punctures are done lower down at lumbar levels to keep the cord safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h2)

question: Which medication is commonly administered intrathecally to treat central nervous system involvement in certain cancers?
explanation: Methotrexate is a frequent intrathecal chemotherapy agent used to reach cancer cells hiding behind the blood-brain barrier. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h3)

question: A patient is scheduled for a surgical procedure on both legs requiring complete lower body numbness without general anesthesia. Which route of administration is the surgical team most likely to select?
explanation: Spinal anesthesia delivered intrathecally provides rapid, profound regional anesthesia for lower body surgeries. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h3)

question: Why are pencil-point spinal needles often preferred over cutting needles?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of infection
options.C: They inject medication twice as fast
options.D: They separate dura fibers rather than cutting them

explanation: Pencil-point needles part the dural fibers, lowering the amount of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and reducing headache risks. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for maintaining strict aseptic technique during an intrathecal procedure?

options.A: Hospital regulations require sterile gear for all injections
options.B: Bacteria will instantly neutralize any local anesthetic injected
options.C: The central nervous system is highly susceptible to severe infections like meningitis
options.D: Skin flora can cause immediate chemical burns inside the spinal canal

explanation: The central nervous system has limited immune defenses, making introduction of pathogens via unsterile technique catastrophic. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: Which body position is most commonly used to prepare a patient for an intrathecal injection?

options.A: Supine position with legs elevated at 45 degrees
options.B: Trendelenburg position with a pillow under the head
options.C: Prone position with arms extended overhead
options.D: Lateral decubitus with knees drawn up to the chest

explanation: Curling into a tight fetal position arches the back and widens the gaps between vertebrae for easier needle access. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h5)

question: During a lumbar puncture, a patient suddenly moves and straightens their legs. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Administer a dose of emergency pain medication
options.B: Immediately pull the spinal needle out to prevent patient injury
options.C: Increase the flow rate of the intravenous fluids
options.D: Gently guide the patient back into the curled position and remind them to stay still

explanation: You got it! Movement can cause complications, so stay calm, help them curl back up gently, and keep that sterile field safe. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why must nurses monitor a patient's blood pressure closely after they get spinal anesthesia?

options.A: Pain medication given intrathecally always increases heart rate
options.B: Lying flat naturally causes sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.C: The body always produces extra blood volume after a spinal injection
options.D: Local anesthetics can block sympathetic nerves and cause significant low blood pressure

explanation: Spot on! Spinal meds can affect the nerves that keep your blood vessels tight, leading to a sudden drop in blood pressure that we need to catch early. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is a recommended nursing intervention to help prevent post-dural puncture headaches?

options.C: Keeping the patient walking for hours

explanation: Adequate hydration helps the body replenish cerebrospinal fluid lost during the procedure. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the main sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It worsens when the patient sits or stands up
options.B: It disappears completely after eating a meal
options.C: It only affects the left side of the forehead
options.D: It is accompanied by sudden high fever

explanation: Brilliant! When the patient sits up, the low fluid pressure pulls on sensitive head structures—making it hurt worse until they lie flat again. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h7)

question: A patient with spinal anesthesia suddenly gasps, struggles to breathe, and cannot speak full sentences. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: The patient drank too much water too quickly after the procedure
options.B: The patient is experiencing a mild panic attack from the bright hospital lights
options.C: The local anesthetic is wearing off too fast
options.D: The anesthetic has spread too high, causing total spinal blockade and breathing muscle paralysis

explanation: Spot on! If the anesthetic travels too high up the spine, it can affect breathing muscles. This is an emergency that needs quick airway support! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h7)
